value: Adopting the lifetime POSIX guard, registered session/lease ownership and a distinct internal interrupted call status turns today's unrecoverable crash state into a bounded, honest settlement for trusted in-process mock execution. That state is an admitted or ended orphan lease, and it permanently occupies the global single slot (v5_tsk_one_lease, unique on active=1). The settlement preserves finished history, consumed budgets, latest cancel/pause/change intent and source stops. interrupted records 'old callback ceased; entry, return and result unknown'. It does not mislabel process death as returned, raised or not_entered. The slice also gives the later ART adoption slice a fenced base: session-bound leases, persisted claim epoch and strict call/reservation/Step validation. That slice will not need to stretch ordinary finish replay into new-epoch adoption. Holding started compose is a useful first dependency, provided the hold is explicit and inspectable (F2). This is not full C13 recovery and claims nothing about generic child or provider safety.
responsibilities: Host guard (shared contract frozen by SOL together with the TSK API): POSIX flock sidecar, canonical DB path/device/inode, session nonce, creator PID for fork refusal, activity permits, close refusal and lifecycle phase. TSK: DB UUID/profile row, session registration, lease-session-claim-epoch binding, register_host/recover/finish_startup, the interrupted status, the C14 state event and replay. TSK remains the sole writer of lease/call/reservation/Step/work state. RUN: uses only the host-constructed managed invoker. Its permit spans admission, the callback and the end_call attempt. It holds no recovery logic and never redispatches an old call. ART/VER: unchanged body/receipt owners. Started compose stays held until a separately frozen ART adoption seam exists, and old-epoch VER never completes a new epoch. MEM: source usability and stops are unchanged; recovery does not need them to prove cessation, and new use passes the existing RUN/admission gates. SOL: owns adoption, integration and final verification. Developers: own internal choices (helper factoring, table layout, error text) without further review.
contract_alignment: C13 recover is aligned, with refinements. It runs at host start only (register_host precedes any claim). Old-runner absence comes from a lock held across the callback lifetime, not from acquisition at open, which respects the C07 warning that lock acquisition alone is not child-termination proof. Owned calls are strictly reconciled before the running epoch is fenced. paused/cancelled persist and a valid open question yields waiting_input. Completed work is not repeated: returned+finished is preserved, and returned-without-Step is never redispatched. Old-epoch VER is not reused, because RUN finalize keys include the new-epoch WorkRef, so fresh VER is required. Same-revision old-epoch ART adoption is explicitly deferred and remains the residual C13 blocker. C15 is aligned: consumed reservations are not refunded; an interrupted call keeps its reservation binding; a fresh call uses a new key (RUN01.model, new lease, index), so no reservation is reused; interrupted is a saved status, never reissued. CHANGE01 is aligned when recover reuses the release settlement rules: latest-only claim, superseded never revives, an old failure never fails the replacement, latest cancel > pause > queued. Section 3 is aligned: BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and the recovery transaction waits on no model or I/O, because ART inspection is deferred. The section 3 startup lock is satisfied for the managed profile only.
findings: F1 HIGH (OWNER-EXCERPTS claim, _authority, admit_call, end_call, release). The session binding must gate every lease-authority path, not only startup. claim's re-claim branch hands the active lease to any caller with the same runner text. _authority and admit_call check the lease id, but not the session. Under the managed profile: claim re-claim, admit_call, begin_step, finish_step, ask, end_call and release must require lease.session == the current active guard session. An old-session lease must be reachable only through recover. Otherwise runner text again acts as proof, contrary to PREPARATION. F2 HIGH (PROPOSAL section 6 compose row, section 4 finish_startup). A held compose lease occupies the global slot, so claim blocks for every Goal, and finish_startup as written refuses entirely. Compose is the main draft path, so this hold will be hit. Staging is still a useful first dependency: it settles the admitted/returned/report/lookup/ask tails and builds the fenced base. However: (a) the held disposition must be a distinct, inspectable result (lease id, Step id, reason), not the same unavailable used for corruption; (b) whether the host may become ready with claims blocked by the existing slot, or stays not-ready, is a developer choice, but it must be fixed in the frozen API and tested; (c) the ART adoption slice should follow next. Note for that slice, not a new criterion: under the lifetime guard and same-DB ART, a C08-key not_found read inside the recovery transaction is definitive for that key. That makes 'no receipt' the cheapest tail. 'Receipt exists' still needs a full producing-call source/purpose recheck and a recovery-provenance binding. F3 HIGH (PROPOSAL section 3, mock_runner MockInvoker.invoke). Pin down the permit lifetime. Acquire the permit before admit_call, so no admitted row exists without one. Release it in finally after the end_call attempt, including the BaseException re-raise path. After close, the session phase is closed and every TSK execution API for that session refuses, so a returned-but-unsaved RUN output cannot begin_step after close. No __del__, GC or atexit path may close the lock FD while permits are outstanding; the registry keeps a strong reference. os.fork duplicates the flock description even when the FD is non-inheritable, so a child keeps the lock. That fails closed, but the PID check must refuse guard use in the child. F4 MEDIUM (C15 reserve_budget; PROPOSAL section 5 step 1). Crashes between reserve_budget and admit_call, or around begin_step, leave consumed reservations that no call binds. Recover must treat them as consumed history: no refund, no rebinding, not corruption, not a reason to hold. Strict link validation applies to reservations that calls reference. F5 MEDIUM (PROPOSAL section 6 table). Enumerate every Action kind. A started verify (RUN finishes it with empty refs) can follow the report rule. A started operate has no EXE recovery (C07 requires EXE.recover first) and must be held or unavailable, never abandoned. Any unlisted kind or status defaults to unavailable. F6 MEDIUM (release both branches, _old_calls, admit_call prior-call loop, end_call, get_call, _questions, RUN retained-ask check). Update each call-status allowlist deliberately. interrupted is terminal and ended without output. It is never equivalent to returned for Step linkage and never blocking like admitted. end_call on an interrupted call returns conflict. An interrupted call with a non-null step is corruption. F7 MEDIUM (release excerpt). Recover's latest-intent disposition should share one private helper with release's superseded and same-revision branches: cancel > pause > drain/queued, old failure never fails the replacement, flags cleared, only safe started Steps abandoned. Recover-only differences are: marking interrupted, the single epoch fence on the latest nonterminal row, guard/session checks, and the exact claim-epoch match. Two divergent copies are the likeliest source of CHANGE01 regressions. F8 MEDIUM (PROPOSAL section 3 durable additions). Avoid migration: store session and claim epoch in a new side table keyed by lease, written in the claim transaction, rather than altering v5_tsk_lease. A missing row means unmanaged, which means unavailable. Read the DB UUID after BEGIN IMMEDIATE in every register/recover transaction and compare it with the guard. Check the PRAGMA database_list main filename against the guard path. Refuse memory, temp and alias connections. Inode checks at open/register suffice against accidental aliasing. F9 LOW (legacy boundary). register_host/recover must fail closed when startup_guard is None or is not an exact registered guard instance; no duck typing. Existing legacy and in-memory tests can therefore never produce interrupted or cessation proof. A pre-RECOVERY01 checkout opening an enrolled DB ignores the enrollment row and could claim. Disclose this as a trusted-operator limit (old PAL is out of scope), not a design defect. F10 LOW (TaskStore._transaction). Use a distinct recover replay namespace. Replay requires a valid guard and DB identity, but not equality with a later startup snapshot. A rejected recover saves no replay because the transaction rolls back, so a same-key retry after fixing the environment is legitimate; state this. The superseded old row keeps its state; only the latest row is fenced. F11 LOW (PROPOSAL section 7). Add cases within existing scope: a SIGSTOPped old owner (alive, lock held) causes refusal; reservation-only crash; started operate and started verify; a same-runner-text claim from another session is refused; begin_step after guard close is refused; a forked child holding the lock blocks recovery.
evidence_limits: Read only the supplied files. Not supplied, so not inspected: the remainder of pal/tasks_v5.py (begin_step, finish_step, ask, get_question_by_key, reserve_budget, register_sources, _required, _registered, _gate, _bind, _headroom, _steps, _set_flags, _mint, _append_event, _lookup_replay/_save_replay, _public, _require_idle, _rollback, get_execution_context, control/complete), artifacts_v5, verification_v5, the MEM owner, CHANGE01-SCOPE, CONTRACT-AUDIT-v5 and the cited tests. TSK/ART/VER method behavior and line references to those files are taken from the proposal and the tails review, not verified. Those documents cite base 175cdc6; this consultation's base is e22c036, and differences between them were not inspected. No code was executed and no tests were run; every test named in the proposal and here is planned. flock semantics on darwin and Linux were not empirically checked. No input hashes were computed. The qualified cessation holds only for trusted synchronous in-process mock callables. It excludes escaped threads, forks, subprocesses, providers, remote calls, external effects and prior CO/AGY calls. Verifier success means structure and size only, not adoption, implementation or product acceptance.
recommendation: REFINE, then adopt. Adopt the lifetime POSIX guard, session/lease ownership with a persisted claim epoch, and internal interrupted status (created only by recover; end_call keeps its three outcomes). Adopt the explicit started-compose hold as a staged first dependency. Fold F1-F8 into the jointly frozen guard+TSK API before independent tests and source; F9-F11 are disclosure and test clarifications. The ended-only fallback is unnecessary unless the real two-process fixture cannot pass. Why the qualified cessation suffices for this slice: the trusted mock callable runs only inside a process holding the guard. The flock is released only at process exit, or by close after all permits have ended. A successor's successful acquisition therefore proves the old callbacks are no longer executing, while their entry and result stay unknown, which is exactly what interrupted records. The full C13 blocker remains: old-epoch ART adoption, absent EXE recovery, and no public finish/complete receipt getter. SOL freezes and verifies; no further blanket review or owner gate is needed for developer technical choices.
